findings.title: Top-level OR fragments are returned without outer parentheses, so composing them gives wrong results
findings.body:
`Prisma.sql` inlines nested fragments verbatim; it does not wrap them in parentheses. Several public methods return a fragment whose top level is an unparenthesized OR:
- `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` / `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` return `(A AND B) OR (C AND D)`.
- `buildFilterConditions` returns `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)` when only one filter is set.
- `getBaseConditions` returns the auth fragment bare when there are no filters.

These methods are the replacement for `findMany`, so callers must embed the fragments in their own queries. A natural pattern is `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "createdAt" >= ${start}`. That parses as `(team branch) OR ((user branch) AND createdAt >= start)`, so date, status or any other extra predicate applies to only one branch. The result is wrong counts and leaked rows outside the requested range.

It is worse with `getFilterConditions()`: `WHERE ${auth} AND ${filter}` becomes `... OR "eventParentId" = X`, which returns rows with that eventParentId regardless of authorization.

The old Prisma where-object API could not be mis-composed this way. Each returned fragment should be wrapped in parentheses, e.g. `Prisma.sql\`(${...})\``, so it is safe to combine.

findings.title: Public `findMany` method removed and constructor contract changed
findings.body:
The public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method is deleted and replaced with `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a raw SQL fragment. All getters now return `Prisma.Sql` instead of `BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput`.

Existing callers of `findMany` or of `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` would break. That includes any code passing the conditions into a Prisma `where`. Those callers would get type errors or, if typed loosely, runtime query failures.

Only the test file is updated in this PR. The PR also says the type-check and test runner were not run successfully. Either confirm there are no other consumers or migrate them in this PR.

findings.title: Unreachable branches in getBaseConditions
findings.body:
`getAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a `Prisma.Sql` object, which is always truthy. Even the NOTHING case is a non-null Sql instance.

As a result, the `else if (filterConditions)` branch and the final `else return NOTHING_CONDITION` can never run. This is harmless today, but it suggests a fallback that does not exist.

If auth were ever made nullable, the `filterConditions`-only branch would silently drop authorization. Simplify to `filterConditions ? (auth) AND (filter) : auth`.

findings.title: Caching tests deleted although caching logic remains
findings.body:
The entire `Caching` describe block was removed, covering both authorization and filter condition caching. The service still caches through `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`.

The cache uses an `=== undefined` sentinel, and `null` is a valid cached filter value. Without these tests, a regression in that logic would go unnoticed. The tests only needed their expectations updated to `Prisma.sql` values, not removal.
